label: letter l input early in the original sequence (positions 0-2)
explanation: Fires only when the input token is the letter l during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase, and only near the start of the sequence. It never fires on any other token, nor on the delimiter or copy phase (including when l is fed back as a copy-phase input). Magnitude decays with position: l at t=0 fires on essentially every occurrence at maximal activation (about 60% of activation mass), l at t=1 fires on nearly all occurrences at roughly half that strength, l at t=2 fires on about two-thirds of occurrences more weakly, t=3 rarely and weakly, and t>=4 essentially never. A repeated l (not the first occurrence in the sequence) almost never fires. Residual misses are weak activations on l at t=3.

issues: Minor: t=2 firing is graded rather than all-or-none. Precision is 0.70 overall, 0.47 when the previous token is a vowel and 0.87 when it is a digit. Adding a vowel condition to the predicate gives test F1 0.9208, which is no better, so this is not a systematic gap the predicate can capture.

Minor: a repeated l does fire about 7.9% of the time (precision 0.079 for in_first==0 in the original phase). These are weak activations, for example 0.24 on l at t=1 right after an l at t=0. 'Almost never' slightly understates this but is fair on mass.

All other claims check out. Activations occur only in the original phase (0 on the delimiter step, 0 of 91k copy-phase l inputs). Every l at t=0 fires (precision 1.0). Every first-occurrence l at t=1 fires (precision 1.0). The t=0, 1 and 2 shares of activation mass (0.60, 0.30, 0.09) match the explanation. Missed activations hold 1.6% of mass and are weak l's at t=3. Test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.907, R 0.936, F1 0.921. Extending the limit to t<=3 lowers F1 to 0.836.
